question: Which of the following statements with respect to position of elements having atomic number 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18 , respectively, in the modern periodic table is INCORRECT?

options.text: These elements belong to the second period of the modern periodic table.
These elements belong to the third period of the modern periodic table.
Electrons in the atoms of these elements are filled in K, L and M shells.
These elements are placed in the same period in the modern periodic table.

solution:
The correct answer is __**These elements belong to the second period of the modern periodic table.**__

 
• **Atomic numbers 11 to 18** correspond to the elements:

 
 
• 11 - Sodium (Na), 12 - Magnesium (Mg), 13 - Aluminium (Al), 14 - Silicon (Si), 15 - Phosphorus (P), 16 - Sulfur (S), 17 - Chlorine (Cl), 18 - Argon (Ar).
 
 
 
• These elements all belong to the **third period** of the periodic table because their outermost electrons occupy the **M shell (n=3)**.
 
• Hence The elements with atomic numbers 11 to 18 belong to the **third period**, not the second.

 
• The Modern periodic law & table was invented by Henry Moseley in 1913. 
 
• The first who was able to arrange all the known elements was Mendeleev, he gave the law called the Mendeleev's periodic law.
 
• Dobereiner grouped the elements into triads.
 
• Newlands gave the law of octaves. 
 
• Modern Periodic Table: 
 
 
• The defects of the periodic table of Mendeleev were sorting out by Henry Moseley who invented the modern periodic law in 1913. 
 
• The law of modern table states that - '' according to the increasing order of their atomic numbers if the elements are arranged, then the element's physical & chemical properties are repeated after regular intervals.
 
 
 
• Salient Features of the Modern Periodic Table: 
 
 
• The element's properties are the functions that are periodical according to their atomic numbers. 
 
• On the basis of the Modern table, Scientist Bohr invented a long form of the periodic table that was created by Warner& Rang. 
 
• The periodic table consists of 18 groups & 7 periods.
 
 
 
• Division structure of elements with respective periods: 
 
 
• According to the increasing order of their atomic numbers if the elements are arranged, then the element's physical & chemical properties are repeated after 2, 8, 18, and 32 intervals. 
 
• There are 2 elements in the first period, 8 elements in second and third periods each respectively, 18 elements fourth and fifth periods each respectively, 32 elements in the sixth period, and 19 elements in the seventh period till now.
